findings.finding: A $3m senior secured convertible note closed around 2026-09-28 (disclosed in a 6-K on 2026-09-29). It converts at 90% of the lowest 10-day VWAP down to a $1.46 per ADS floor and pays make-whole interest on conversion. With spot at $3.93, far below the $7.30 fixed price, the holder can convert and sell ADSs on every session, including 2026-10-05. At about $3.5 per ADS, $3m is about 850k ADSs, against roughly 100k ADSs ($378k-451k) of daily turnover.
findings.mechanism_in_window: Conversion notices can be delivered on any trading day and converted ADSs sold the same session. The note has been outstanding since about 2026-09-28, so this selling runs through the window rather than at a later date. ADSs issued for the 2026-10-01 interest payment (12% if paid in shares) are also sellable inside the window.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Since the 6-K on 2026-09-29, next-close moves after drops ran +25.9% (from 09-29), then -26.8% on 10-01 and -5.5% on 10-02 (baseline events). The name alternates violently. Of the last 12 comparable falls, 7 were followed by a rise, and the median absolute next-close move was about 7%.
findings.why_not_priced: The fall prices dilution to date, not dilution still to come. Under a lowest-10-day-VWAP formula, each lower print lowers the next conversion price, so supply grows as the price falls, and with no floor event yet (spot is about 2.7x the $1.46 floor) the mechanism is still live. If the market had fully priced this, volume would not be ordinary at 1.47x, because a finished seller usually shows as a capitulation spike.
findings.independence: Serial ADS ratio changes (F-6 POS on 2026-07-14 and 2026-09-10) and going-concern language in the 20-F of 2026-04-30 show repeated dilution: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1806524/000095012726000092/f-6pos.htm
